page.overview:
Who is Fei Long?

Fei Long is Capcom's tribute to the Wing Chun and Jeet Kune Do movie legend Bruce Lee as Fei Long's overall appearance is modeled after Lee's iconic role as Chén Zhēn the Chinese Jīngwǔ Prodigy during the dojo crowd-fight scene from 1972's [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fist_of_Fury Fist of Fury Part I: The Chinese Connection] originally titled in Hong Kong as Jīngwǔ Mén (精武門; literally: "Pure-Martial School"), a movie in which the secondary antagonist Petrov the Russian Strongman Sensei of who would become one of the character models for Eagle.

Not only do the two look alike and come from the same city, Fei Long also lets out similar battle cries to Lee, and is just as furious and fast. Also, Fei Long (飛龍) is Chinese for "flying dragon", as well as a type of kick. Bruce Lee's Chinese screen name was 李小龍 (Lǐ Xiǎolóng in Mandarin and Lee Siu-lung in his preferred Cantonese); the latter two characters meaning "little dragon".

There are a few differences between Fei Long and Lee; Bruce Lee lived in the United States of America since he was 18 and had an American wife who he had a son and a daughter with, whereas Fei Long has no apparent connection to the West, is not shown to be married or in a relationship, and doesn't have any children of his own.

Also (although he is seen using them in one of his Super Street Fighter II win poses and in some of his artwork), unlike Bruce Lee, Fei Long never actually uses nunchaku as a weapon or a special move, but instead he only uses them to display his skills in front of cameras. Fei Long also bears a notable resemblance to Kenshiro from the Fist of the North Star manga and anime series.
